record.paper_title: Separability of Topological Groups: A Survey with Open Problems
record.original_question: Characterize the Tychonoff spaces X for which every closed vector subspace of C_p(X) is separable, where C_p(X) denotes the space of all continuous real-valued functions on X endowed with the topology of pointwise convergence.

evidence.quote: Let C_p(X,E) denote the space of all continuous E-valued functions on X endowed with the pointwise convergence topology.
Characterize those Tychonoff spaces X such that all closed vector subspaces of C_p(X) are separable.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a Tychonoff (i.e. completely regular Hausdorff) topological space $X$, let $C_p(X)$ denote the vector space of all continuous real-valued functions on $X$ equipped with the topology of pointwise convergence (the subspace topology inherited from the product space $\mathbb{R}^X$). A topological space is called separable if it contains a countable dense subset. By a closed vector subspace of $C_p(X)$ we mean a linear subspace that is closed in the pointwise convergence topology.

Give an intrinsic topological characterization of those Tychonoff spaces $X$ with the property that every closed vector subspace of $C_p(X)$ is separable.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is stated as an open problem in a survey on separability of topological groups. Related partial results exist: it is known that the Michael line $\mathbb{M}$ yields a separable $C_p(\mathbb{M})$ containing a nonseparable closed vector subspace, and various sufficient/necessary conditions involving functionally countable P-spaces and pseudocompactness have been investigated. No complete intrinsic characterization has been located in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Nonseparable closed vector subspaces of separable topological vector spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies nonseparable closed vector subspaces of separable C_p(X), e.g. for the Michael line.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist showing C_p(X) can be separable while containing nonseparable closed vector subspaces, but no full characterization is given.

status_evidence.title: On subspaces of spaces C_p(X) isomorphic to c_0 and ℓ_q
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates structure of closed subspaces of C_p(X).
status_evidence.claim: Continuing research on closed subspaces of C_p(X) suggests the characterization remains an open problem.
